footprint.notes: Disney's FY2026 10-K (fiscal year ended Oct 3, 2026) gives employees only as U.S. versus outside the U.S. (173,000 and 61,000 of about 234,000); it does not break out employees, investment or taxes by state or country. Sites are the parks and resorts as described in the FY2026 10-K (Item 1, Experiences) plus the Burbank property from Item 2. Hong Kong and Shanghai are joint ventures (Disney 48% and 43%); Tokyo Disney Resort is licensed and owned by Oriental Land Co. The 10-K also names Disney Lookout Cay at Lighthouse Point (about 600 acres on Eleuthera, Bahamas) and a planned Miral-built, Disney-licensed resort in Abu Dhabi; neither is listed as a site. Not checked: Disney-commissioned economic impact studies of individual resorts (e.g. Walt Disney World in Florida), which would be tier company-commissioned. Revenue by geography is in the records and not repeated.

source.label: 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A), CEO Pay Ratio
source.quote: The median Disney employee works in a full-time hourly role in parks and has been with the Company for over eight years. For fiscal 2025, the median employee’s total annual compensation was $56,932.

pay.notes: Employees: approximate head count at fiscal year end 2026 (October 3, 2026), including part-time and seasonal staff. Payroll: the FY2026 10-K discloses no total staff cost, so the CEO pay ratio median from the January 2026 proxy is used. It is the median for fiscal 2025 (workforce reviewed as of September 26, 2025; base salary, overtime and the company's health-insurance contribution); the fiscal 2026 median will appear only in the proxy due in January 2027. The CEO pay ratio for fiscal 2025 was 805:1.
